metadata.title: Decisions of Number Guessing Game
metadata.description: Subjects were asked to play a game named "Number Guessing". In the game subjects needed to figure out a integer random number in the range of 1-1000 by ask two types of question. A web-based applicaiton was deployed for data collection. Each subject's decisions (the chosen numbers) for searching targeted number were recorded.

metadata.title: CONNECTED DOMSATURATION NUMBER OF A GRAPH
metadata.description: In general, a set S of vertices of a graph G is said to be saturated by an rnatching M (where a matching M in G is a set of independent edges) if every vertex of S is incident to some edge of M. In domsaturation the concept of domination is in introduced. The domsaturation number, ds of a graph G is defined to be the least positive integer k such that every vertex of G lies in a dominating set of cardinality k. A graph G consists of a pair (V(G) , E(G)) where V(G) is a non-empty finite set whose elements are called points or vertices and E(G) is a set of unordered pairs of distinct elements of V(G). The elements of E(G) are called lines or edges of the graph G. A graph with p points and q lines is called a (p, q) graph.

metadata.title: Omega Numbers: Symmetries and Infinitary Regularization in a Graded Transarchimedean Extension of Complex Analysis
metadata.description:
Starting from the standard Hahn/Laurent-series construction over \(\mathbb{C}\) with value group \(\mathbb{Z}\), we introduce the \emph{Omega number system}, a graded transarchimedean interpretation and extension of complex arithmetic designed to represent finite, infinitesimal, and infinitary quantities within a common algebraic setting. The construction is organized around a distinguished infinitary scale \(\Omega\), which may be realized concretely as the hyperreal equivalence class of the sequence \((1,2,3,\dots)\) under an ultrapower construction. A lifting function \(L^\Omega(n)\), indexed by \(n\in\mathbb{Z}\), separates the classical complex component at grade \(0\), infinitary magnitudes at positive grades, and infinitesimal magnitudes at negative grades.
 
Within this graded setting we distinguish the absolute zero \(\underline{0}\), the infinitesimal almost-zero class \(\overline{0}\), and its canonical member \(0^*=\Omega^{-1}\). Together, \(\underline{0}\cup\overline{0}\) refines the classical zero of real and complex analysis into a continuum-cardinality graded near-zero class. We develop additive linear and exponential model families, introduce a multiplicative product-lifting model motivated by Dirichlet-type expansions, establish uniqueness of graded representation and basic valuation laws, and describe rank-lifted model families generated by higher-order infinitary base elements \(^{r}\Omega\). These constructions provide a formal setting in which infinitesimal and infinitary contributions can be compared, reflected, shifted, and separated by grade.
 
We then study selected elementary functions and zeta-type expressions in the Omega domain. Periodic functions at infinitary arguments admit natural ultralimit or distributional interpretations, while divergent or asymptotic expressions may be decomposed into finite, infinitesimal, and infinitary graded components. We also introduce an \(\Omega\)-operator toolkit on the graded basis, including grade shifts, reflection, parity, and phase twists. In particular, the reflection operator exchanges infinitesimal and infinitary grades and leads to conditional \(\Omega\)-reflection principles for zeta-type expressions paralleling the classical functional equation across grades. The present paper develops the formal graded construction and illustrative examples; fuller analytic, operator-algebraic, and application-oriented extensions are left for future work.

metadata.title: Cyrtomenus (Cyrtomenus) mirabilis Perty
metadata.description:
Cyrtomenus (Cyrtomenus) mirabilis (Perty)

Cydnus mirabilis Perty, 1830: 166.

Cyrtomenus mutabilis Dallas, 1851: 112; Walker, 1867: 147. Usage of the spelling mutabilis appears to be due to an error on the caption of the plate accompanying the original description of Cydnus mirabilis (Froeschner 1981).

Cyrtomenus mirabilis: Stål 1876: 18; Distant, 1880: 3; Signoret, 1881: 199; Lethierry & Severin, 1893: 62; Breddin, 1904: 407.

Macroscytus umbonatus Berg, 1878: 14; syn. by Signoret, 1881.

New synonym.

metadata.title: Las dos mitades de Jacob Riis: un estudio comparativo de su obra literaria y fotográfica. Sociedad Latina de Comunicación Social, colección Cuadernos de Bellas Artes, vols. 28 y 29.
metadata.description:
Las dos mitades de Jacob Riis ocupa un espacio inédito en la serie de aproximaciones de que ha sido objeto el autor de Cómo vive la otra mitad. Se trata de un estudio que pretende no solo abarcar por separado la génesis de las dos mitades, literaria y fotográfica, de la obra del reformista danés, sino demostrar que el diálogo entre esos dos lenguajes supone un elemento de fuerza crítica y constructiva de dimensiones no superadas en el contexto de la denuncia promovida por el periodismo muckraker, la ficción naturalista y la fotografía documental de finales del siglo XIX y principios del XX. Así, en el primer volumen se analiza la “mitad literaria” de la obra de Riis: mantiene vínculos con la literatura popular y reformista decimonónica y participa a su vez de las nuevas corrientes de la literatura moderna, interesadas en el retrato fiel de los problemas sociales (desde Stephen Crane hasta Jack London o Upton Sinclair). El hecho de que la ficción y la crónica periodística (o su registro gráfico) sean casi intercambiables pone de relieve la dimensión política antes que estética de la literatura americana. En el segundo volumen se presenta la “mitad fotográfica” de la obra de Riis. El olvido al que estuvieron relegadas sus imágenes durante casi cuarenta años y el modo tan vertiginoso en que se las recuperó nos llevan a estudiar el tratamiento que ha recibido en la historia del medio fotográfico y a plantear una comparación con otras iniciativas coetáneas, lo que nos permite subrayar su carácter pionero e inédito.

En contraste con las lecturas reduccionistas de los Estudios Culturales y con la asimilación deformada o incompleta de Riis en la historiografía fotográfica, Las dos mitades aspira a ser el mayor esfuerzo comprensivo de la figura del autor desde el punto de vista de la complejidad y versatilidad de los ideales americanos que han supuesto un marco de interpretación capaz de ratificar la vigencia de sus intenciones. América, como ha señalado la crítica, es un texto no escrito y, podríamos añadir, un lugar no revelado o fotografiado. En la medida en que las imágenes de Riis señalaban un déficit de civilización, la fe humanista que le movía a mostrarlas y darles voz nacía de la necesidad sentida de luchar por el país que, contra las apariencias, aún representaba una esperanza para el mundo. La calidad de esa representación preside el esfuerzo por devolver a la obra de Riis, más allá de sus mitades, un valor de lectura que se corresponda con la unidad de las más nobles aspiraciones de la ciudadanía.

metadata.title: Knowledge Graph Industry Benchmarking Survey - 2022
metadata.description:
The objective of this industry study was to capture baseline statistics on the size, nature and direction of data management using semantic standards or in other words the capabilities that result from having a knowledge graph.

What is the Premise?

The adoption of knowledge graphs has been steadily rising across several information-intensive industry sectors including those in Healthcare and Life Sciences, Financial Services and Industry. This sign of maturity is one of the conclusions from the 2nd Annual Knowledge Graph Benchmarking Study – conducted jointly by the Enterprise Knowledge Graph Foundation (EKGF) and the Knowledge Graph Conference (KGC).

What does “Knowledge Graph Industry Survey Report” include?

  • Benchmarking Profiles
  • Maturity, Drivers, Use Cases and Inhibitors
  • Industry Capabilities
  • Key Takeaways

metadata.title: ionicf/graph-count-disconnected-communities: Count the number of disconnected communities in a graph, for the given community membership of each vertex
metadata.description:
Count the number of disconnected communities in a graph, for the given community membership of each vertex.

# Count disconnected communities in the web-Stanford graph, from given the membership (keyed, starting from 0).
$ graph-count-disconnected-communities -k -r 0 -i web-Stanford.mtx -m web-Stanford-membership.txt

# Count disconnected communities in the web-Stanford graph, from given the membership file (in TSV format).
$ graph-count-disconnected-communities -k -r 0 -i web-Stanford.mtx -m web-Stanford-membership.tsv -f mtx

# Count disconnected communities in the weighted vt2010 graph, from given the membership file (in CSV format).
$ graph-count-disconnected-communities -k -r 0 -i vt2010.mtx -m vt2010-membership.csv -w

<br>

Usage

$ graph-count-disconnected-communities [options]

Options:
  -h, --help                    Show this help message.
  -i, --input <file>            Input file name.
  -f, --input-format <format>   Input file format.
  -m, --membership <file>       Community membership file name.
  -k, --membership-keyed        Community membership file is keyed.
  -r, --membership-start        Community membership start index.
  -w, --weighted                Input graph is weighted.
  -s, --symmetric               Input graph is symmetric.

Supported formats:
  mtx       Matrix Market format (default).
  coo       Coordinate format.
  edgelist  Edgelist format.
  csv       Comma-separated values format.
  tsv       Tab-separated values format.

<br>

Installation

$ git clone https://github.com/ionicf/graph-count-disconnected-communities
$ cd graph-count-disconnected-communities
$ ./install.sh --prefix /usr/local

<br> <br>

<br>
